method: 30 random links per source (seed 7, pipeline/scale/spotcheck.py), each judged by reading the quoted source field/title/conditions: is the link true as labelled?

trials_gene_first_build.note: loose symbol matching (somatic cancer studies, acronyms such as HBB=Helping Babies Breathe, NHS=Natural History Study, drug codes DCC-3116, anti-LRP4, SNP studies). Rules rewritten (gene-context requirement, acronym detector, no oncology studies).

asset_simons.note: Every item is a gene symbol line on the Simons list. All diseases of that gene are credited (rule list_item_gene). At disease level some are sibling phenotypes outside Simons' neurodevelopmental focus (e.g. CACNA1C -> Brugada 3 / long QT 8; SMARCA4 -> otosclerosis 12), so the UI must say 'studies <GENE>'.

asset_citizen.note: the same gene-level caveat as Simons applies (CACNA1A -> SCA6, SMC1A -> CdLS 2)

org_clinicaltrials.gov_intermediate.first_build: before the focused-trial and relevance rules, one multi-condition registry linked single collaborators to ~228 diseases, and funders and professional bodies (e.g. 'Portuguese Football Federation') passed. Both were fixed before this sample.

errors.1: borderline: VHL Alliance -> pheochromocytoma (true for VHL-associated pheo, but VHL Alliance is not a pheochromocytoma group)

org_clinicaltrials.gov.note: final rules: org name must share a distinctive token with the disease; gene-via links also need the trial's conditions to share a phenotype word with the disease. An intermediate sample (24/30) had CTNNB1 Foundation -> sibling phenotypes, ALS Association -> HD / semantic dementia via multi-condition trials, and a person's name used as an org label. All are fixed.
